claims.text: The meta-analysis included 32 randomized studies with 6089 participants.

claims.text: Short-term depressive symptoms improved compared with control conditions (Hedges g 0.29, 95% CI 0.20–0.38).

sources.title: Digital interventions to reduce social isolation and loneliness in older adults: An evidence and gap map

provenance.access_note: AI-prepared paraphrase from accessible web research text; human claim review pending. Direct B-04 attempt: manual_review; web page request was blocked with HTTP 403
provenance.license_note: Reuse terms not yet reviewed. Only short paraphrases and source metadata are included; do not infer redistribution permission.

references.locator: Plain-language summary: What studies are included?; What are the main findings?; How up-to-date is this EGM?

claims.text: The map contains 200 articles: 97 systematic reviews and 103 primary studies. Most evidence comes from high-income settings and none from low-income countries.
Community-level outcomes and process measures are rarely reported. Included work does not assess affordability or lack of accessibility, and adverse effects are seldom reported.
More than 70% of the included systematic reviews were rated critically low quality.

limitations.text: Searches extended through May 2021; this is not a current exhaustive map.
A map describes coverage and gaps, not a pooled intervention effect.

JMIR Publications, 2017-06-06. DOI 10.2196/mental.7785. This record contains new paraphrases, not verbatim full text.

references.locator: Abstract: Methods and Results; author affiliations and study limitations

claims.text: The unblinded randomized study enrolled 70 young adults. The Woebot arm showed a greater reduction in PHQ-9 depressive symptoms than the information-only control after two weeks.
population_scope: Adults aged 18–28 recruited from a university community

claims.text: Anxiety decreased in both groups in the completer analysis; this does not establish a differential anxiety benefit for Woebot.
population_scope: Adults aged 18–28 recruited from a university community

limitations.text: Short follow-up, unblinded allocation and a university sample limit transferability to older adults.
Seventeen percent did not provide follow-up data; a study author was affiliated with Woebot Labs.

claims.text: Among 4517 paying users, anxiety and depression scores fell during the first two weeks. Anxiety gains persisted over the following two weeks, while depression scores rose slightly.
population_scope: Paying Youper users who consented to research use of their data

claims.text: Week-four retention was 1927 of 4517 users (42.66%). Retention and app ratings do not establish clinical effectiveness.
population_scope: Paying Youper users who consented to research use of their data

limitations.text: Paying-user selection, attrition and lack of randomized comparison limit causal conclusions.
Several authors were affiliated with Youper; older-adult applicability requires separate assessment.
